request.spec:
A steward can merge a person into another (a select of the other person and a merge button on
the row; PERSON_MERGED from=<name> into=<name>; anyone else, the same person, or either of them
retired, is refused with an error on the row). The merged person's claims move to the other
(numbers and dates kept, listed after the other's claims in the order they were added, each losing
any figure a statement bound); the merged name and aliases become aliases of the other; the merged
person's patrons are added to the other's (not themselves, no repeats), anyone naming the merged
person as patron names the other instead (no repeats), and the merged person's pool memberships move
to the other (shares added when the other is already a member). Their statements, holds, watchers
and contact are dropped. The merged person leaves the list (no row), and every total follows.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can merge a person into another (a select of the other person and a merge button on
the row; PERSON_MERGED from=<name> into=<name>; anyone else, the same person, or either of them
retired, is refused with an error on the row). The merged person's claims move to the other
(numbers and dates kept, listed after the other's claims in the order they were added, each losing
any figure a statement bound); the merged name and aliases become aliases of the other; the merged
person's patrons are added to the other's (not themselves, no repeats), anyone naming the merged
person as patron names the other instead (no repeats), and the merged person's pool memberships move
to the other (shares added when the other is already a member). Their statements, holds, watchers

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've added person merge, and `bin/e2e` now passes all 4 tests: the merge test and the three existing scenarios. Before my change the merge test failed and the other three passed.

**How it works**
- **Where it lives:** a new migration (`V67__person_merged.sql`) adds a `merged_into` column to `person`. The merge logic is in `PersonMergeService`, called through `POST /api/sheets/{sheet}/people/{id}/merge` with `{intoId}`. Totals are tracked the same way as other changes, so the audit gets `PERSON_MERGED from=… into=…` followed by any `ROLLUP`/`TOTALS` lines.
- **The merged person is kept, not deleted.** Their row is marked as merged, and the sheet's person lookups (the list, find-by-id and find-by-name) ignore marked rows. That one change makes the person leave the list, totals, quick-add and paste. I didn't delete the row because many history tables reference it.
- **Who is refused:** anyone who isn't a steward, merging a person into themselves, or either person being retired. A refusal shows `person-error` on the row and writes nothing.
- **What moves:**
  - **Claims** move with their numbers and dates kept and any figure a statement bound removed. They are re-listed one at a time in the order they were added, so they show above the other person's existing claims, which is the order the test expects.
  - **Name and aliases** become aliases of the other person.
  - **Patrons:** the merged person's patrons are added to the other's, skipping the other person themselves and any repeats. Anyone who named the merged person as patron now names the other, again without repeats or self-patronage.
  - **Pools:** memberships move to the other person; where they were already a member, the shares are added together.
  - **Dropped:** the merged person's statements, holds, watchers and contact.
- **Screen:** each row has a "Merge into" select (`person-merge-into`) and a Merge button (`person-merge`). After a merge the screen re-reads people and claims.

**Things to know**
- The merged person's name stays reserved on the sheet. A new person called "Ben" can't be added afterwards, and the alias would block it anyway.
- Viewing the sheet as of a past date no longer shows the merged person at all, even for days before the merge.
- Merged pool shares aren't capped at 100. They can go over it until they reach 999.99, the largest value the column holds.
